probes.description: Against a server that speaks MCP 2026-07-28, send a legacy initialize handshake. A dual-era server that still accepts it runs a second authorization path, and on the legacy path authorization was established once at initialize rather than per request. The era is chosen by the client, so this is a downgrade path unless the legacy path enforces per-request authorization and has a documented sunset.

assertions.description: A modern server should decline the legacy initialize handshake (or enforce per-request authorization on it)

corroboration.description: Finding only when the legacy handshake was accepted

remediation: If the legacy (initialize / Mcp-Session-Id) path must remain during migration, enforce per-request authorization on it exactly as on the stateless path, inventory it, and give it a documented sunset date. Otherwise set a minimum supported version and decline initialize, naming the supported versions in the error (CoSAI MCP Security v2.0 §3.2.12 and MCP-T7).
